name: SwiftProtobuf (binary wire format)
baseline: Codable with Foundation JSONEncoder / JSONDecoder (swift-foundation, macOS 15.7.2)
verdict_reason: A third-party benchmark (Apache Fory's Swift suite) measured 5.1x-19.4x the throughput of JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder across six data shapes, with payloads 42-50% smaller. The swift-protobuf README itself only says the serializers are 'extensively optimized'.
tier_reason: Benchmark code and run script (swift build -c release) are public in apache/fory, the page states OS build, core count and memory, and the authors are independent of swift-protobuf.
claimed_speedup: Throughput vs JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder: NumericStruct serialize 7,572,190 vs 481,278 ops/s (15.7x), deserialize 7,317,942 vs 377,802 (19.4x); MediaContent serialize 784,863 vs 111,200 (7.1x), deserialize 549,726 vs 97,799 (5.6x); MediaContentList deserialize 99,445 vs 19,521 (5.1x) (ratios derived from page data). Size: 93 vs 159 bytes (NumericStruct), 301 vs 608 bytes (MediaContent).
workload: Serialize and deserialize six model shapes (struct of 12 int32 fields, mixed struct with arrays, nested media object graph, and lists of each) for 3 s per case; the protobuf path includes converting between the Swift models and generated message types
metric: throughput (operations per second) and payload size
hardware: MacBook Pro, 12 logical cores, 48 GB (chip not named)
toolchain: swift build -c release (run.sh); Swift version not stated; swift-protobuf 1.35.0 or later
install: Swift Package Manager (plus the protoc-gen-swift plugin)
one_liner: Apple's Protocol Buffers runtime for Swift; 5-19x the throughput of Codable JSON in a third-party benchmark, at about half the bytes.
how_it_is_fast: protoc generates a concrete serializer for each message type, so encoding and decoding are straight-line visits over numbered fields in a varint and length-delimited wire format. There are no key strings to write, match or hash, no Codable container existentials, and no text escaping or number formatting.
use_it_when: Wire or disk formats where you control both ends
Hot paths encoding many small structs
skip_it_when: Payloads must be human-readable or match an existing JSON API
You cannot add a code-generation step to the build
caveats: Measured by a competing serialization project (Apache Fory), which ranks first in its own table.
The protobuf numbers include converting to and from generated message types, which understates SwiftProtobuf's raw speed.
CPU model not named; one run of 3 s per case.
tradeoffs: Generated message types instead of your own structs, or a conversion layer
Schema files and a protoc plugin in the build

evidence.quote: Performant: The binary and JSON serializers have been extensively optimized.
